meta.title: The PERFECT Vietnam Itinerary | Travel Guide 2026 🇻🇳
meta.description:
Planning a trip to Vietnam in 2026? This is our complete, tried-and-tested Vietnam itinerary designed to help you see the highlights—from the misty mountains of Sapa to the bustling streets of Ho Chi Minh City—without burning out.

After spending a full month traveling from North to South, we’re sharing exactly where to go, which experiences are worth the hype, and how to structure your route for the best experience. We recommend starting in Hanoi and working your way down to Saigon.

In this video, we cover:
-Hanoi & Ha Long Bay: Why you should splurge on your cruise and where to stay in the Old Quarter.
-Sapa: Navigating the "infamous" sleeper buses and chasing the fog in the northern mountains.
-Hanoi Train Street: How to safely visit this bucket-list spot.
-Central Vietnam: Choosing between the beach vibes of Da Nang and the ancient charm of Hoi An.
-Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon): Hidden gems, the Cafe Apartments, and essential day trips like the Cu Chi Tunnels.

CHAPTERS
(0:00-0:49) The Perfect Vietnam Route (North to South)
(0:50-3:22) Part 1: Ha Long Bay Cruise, Overnight Bus to Sapa, Hanoi
(3:23-4:02) Part 2: Central Vietnam (Da Nang and Hoi An)
(4:03-5:16) Part 3: Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) & Day Trips: Cu Chi Tunnels & Mekong Delta

transcript: There is way too much to do in Vietnam,  and that's exactly why it ends up on so   many bucket lists. This is a country that  somehow delivers vibrant, high energy cities,   stunning beaches, and misty mountain towns  all in one trip. Honestly, it can almost feel   overwhelming. If you're planning a visit, you've  probably caught yourself asking questions like,   "Where do I start? Where do I end? And is it  really worth going 6 hours out of the way for   that one spot everyone keeps talking about?" We  spent a full month traveling through Vietnam,   testing the must-sees, chasing the highlights,  and figuring out which experiences truly lived   up to the hype and which ones didn't. This is  our full Vietnam itinerary built to help you   plan an incredible trip without burning out. Take  what fits your travel style, skip what doesn't,   and let us know in the comments which stops you're  adding to your list. We recommend starting in   the north and making your way down to the busy  south, which is a bit more forgiving if you're   feeling some jet lag or culture shock at the  start of your trip. We recommend flying into   Hanoi and starting with a relaxing Ha Long  Bay cruise. There are many cruises offered   from budget friendly boats to high-end luxury  ships. Our recommendation is to actually pick   one that's a little above your normal budget.  You'll get a lot of luxury for an incredible   value and you won't regret the experience. Spend  your first days in Vietnam basking in the sun,   watching the gorgeous limestone islands float by,  and savoring some amazing food without needing to   check for views. No need to book accommodation  in Ha Long Bay either. The cruises are the   main attraction in the area, and many offer  transportation to and from Hanoi directly. Now that you started off your trip on the right  foot and hopefully are adjusted to the time zone,   it's time to spend a few days in the northern  mountain town of Sapa. This is a great time   to try out the famous or maybe infamous  back that's disgusting. It's overnight   buses. Once you're in Sapa, spend your  days and nights walking the streets and   watching the fog roll in and out. Enjoy the  amazing food scene where the flavors you'll   experience are way different from the rest  of the country. For our adrenaline junkies,   check out the Sunworld Fanipan Legend Cable  Car. We have two full videos on Sapa as this   was our favorite place in Vietnam. So, go check  those out if you want more on this amazing town. After your mountain adventures, it's time to  spend a few days in Hanoi. If you're looking   for a true to Vietnam experience, we recommend  the Old Quarter or French Quarter as potential   home bases. These put you in the center  of the action. You'll learn how to cross   the streets full of full-speed motorbikes in  the Old Quarter, but also to be able to find   quieter corners of the city in the French  Quarter. In addition to people watching,   some additional must dos in the area  are the Ha Lo Prison, Hoam Kiem Lake,   and the Tron Quac Pagoda. If you find yourself  getting used to the chaos of Hanoi and are   seeking an even greater thrill, then it's time  for you to check out Hanoi's train street. Book with a local cafe beforehand to secure your  spot for this once in a lifetime experience. Now, if you want to enjoy the Hanoi chaos  but from a distance, the neighborhood of   West Lake might be more your speed. It's a more  western feeling area situated around Lake Tay Ho,   but is around a 20-minute drive from some  of the activities that we just mentioned.   It's a great place to spring for a  luxury hotel stay like L7 by Lotte. After your time in Hanoi, it's time to  downshift and head to central Vietnam   to visit Da Nang and Hoi An. These two towns  are about a 25-minute drive from each other,   so you really only have to pick one to stay in.  Da Nang is more of a beach town with a vibrant   nightlife and a more laid-back, sleepy daytime  atmosphere. Hoi An is more of a cultural hub,   famous for its occasional massive flooding. Make  sure to check what season you're going to make   sure that you'll be able to participate in all the  activities that you want to do. In the dry season,   it's a great place to wander the ancient town  streets and peruse local arts and crafts. It's   a touristy stop, but a gorgeous one at that.  There are also events held on the riverfront,   and we were lucky enough to catch New Year's  Eve there, which is a memory we'll never forget. At this point, you'll be feeling like a pro  traveler, and it's time to put it to the test   by heading south one more time to Ho Chi Minh  City, aka Saigon. Vietnam's largest city is   at the same time more chaotic and more structured  than Hanoi, but brings a whole new energy. We have   a full Ho Chi Minh City guide on our channel, so  make sure you check out that video for specifics,   but we recommend at least 3 days here to see  all the city has to offer, plus one day trip.   While exploring the city, don't miss some  famous spots like the cafe apartments and   the Independence Palace and some more hidden gems  too like Tao Dan Park and the Saigon Sky Deck.   Some day trips that we recommend are to the Cu  Chi Tunnels or to the Mekong River Delta region. And that brings us to the end of our recommended  Vietnam itinerary. We hope this helped bring a   little clarity to what's worth prioritizing and  where to focus your time. Vietnam is incredibly   rich in culture, history, and natural beauty.  And honestly, it was hard to narrow it down   this much. Check out our channel for more Vietnam  videos and deep dives. And make sure to subscribe   because we have a lot more videos on Asia travel  coming up. There are so many amazing places we   couldn't include. So, if you have favorites or  hidden gems, drop them in the comments. We'd love   to hear them. Thanks so much for watching. Happy  trip planning and we'll see you in the next one.
